findings.description: The cycle guard on the __cause__ walk was removed, so the loop now only terminates when the chain reaches an exception with no cause. A cyclic __cause__ chain would loop forever.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an exception whose __cause__ chain loops back on itself (e.g. a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, which Python allows by manual assignment), raised inside a retried function with retry_if_exception_cause_type configured. Mechanism: the while condition at line 180 never sees exc become None or a seen object, so it spins indefinitely without advancing to a terminal state. Impact: the retry predicate hangs the calling thread instead of returning a decision.
